chapter: Minton's, Louis Armstrong and the South
title: Jim Chapin's book on his style
summary: Jim Chapin wrote a book on Clarke's left-hand and foot work that sold worldwide, with no royalties for Clarke, though drummers needed to see it to believe it.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: One drummer who liked it, Jim Chapin, who liked it so much he wrote a book, and that opened the whole thing up to everybody.
Really? Wrote a book about the the drumming?
He wrote all the things I was doing.
Oh, you mean he produced a book on the drumming.
Oh, and then it was open to people.
Those books are sold all over the world.
Do you get the royalties on it?
No. I didn't get anything at all.

Just wrote about how Kenny Clarke developed this style of playing and so forth and all that, and -- but what he did, he wrote the left hand and the foot, you know, and showed drummers how to use their foot. But it's hard to -- to write a book about things like that, for people who read the book to understand.
So therefore, they still didn't believe in it.
: Until they got exposed to it.
And then they began to understand.
What he was trying to convey.
